title: Fiji Small-Ship Cruise in 6 Days: Three Nights Through the Yasawa and Mamanuca Islands
meta_title: Fiji Small-Ship Cruise: 3 Nights in the Yasawa Islands
meta_description: 6-day Fiji cruise holiday: a 3-night all-inclusive small-ship cruise to Modriki, Soso village and the Sacred Isles, with a night in Nadi either side.
hero_alt: A small ship anchored off a Fijian island
tagline: Wake up at a different island every morning
facts: Transfers and a small cruise ship
intro: A small Fijian ship carries about 60 guests on a 3-night cruise from Port Denarau through the outer Mamanuca and Yasawa Islands, anchoring each night at a quiet island. Days are for snorkelling, beaches, a Fijian village and a Sunday church service with singing you will not forget; meals, shore trips and snorkel gear are included. The cruise sails on Friday afternoon and returns on Monday afternoon. We have added a night in Nadi on both sides: arriving the day before protects you from a late flight, and the ship returns too late for most flights home on the same day.

best_time: May to October is the dry season: sunny, less humid and the best time for the islands; July and the school holidays are busiest. November to April is hot and wet, with a risk of cyclones from December to March.

faqs.q: What days does the cruise run?
faqs.a: The 3-night cruise leaves on Friday and returns on Monday. Longer 4- and 7-night cruises to the northern Yasawas run on other days.
The ship sails mostly inside sheltered reefs and anchors at night. Sensitive travellers should bring tablets.
Yes, from about 7 years. The ship has a pool, and the crew run activities.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Fiji dollars
good_to_know.text: Fiji uses the Fiji dollar. Cards work in resorts, Denarau and Nadi; carry small cash for villages, markets and tips. Resort prices on the islands are high, so plan for meals there.

good_to_know.title: Village etiquette
good_to_know.text: In a Fijian village, cover shoulders and knees (a sarong is fine), take off hats and sunglasses, never touch anyone's head, and wait to be invited in. Visitors bring a small gift of kava root (sevusevu); your guide arranges it. Sunday is for church and rest in the villages.

good_to_know.title: Sun and sea
good_to_know.text: The tropical sun is strong: use reef-safe sunscreen and a rash vest. Swim and snorkel only where your resort or crew says it is safe, wear reef shoes, and do not touch or stand on coral.

good_to_know.title: Fiji time
good_to_know.text: Life is relaxed. Boats and transfers run to timetables but may change with the weather; build in time and keep the day of your flight home free.

emergency: Suva, Viti Levu (contact details in your travel pack)
dining_intro: Almost 4 in 10 Fijians have Indian roots, so dal, roti, curries and Indian sweets are everywhere on Viti Levu, and resorts on the main island cook vegetarian food well. Island resorts and boats need your dietary brief in advance; we send it to each one.
dining_avoid: Kokoda (raw fish in coconut), lovo (earth-oven meat) and many coconut sauces with fish are local favourites. Ask for the vegetable lovo or Indian vegetarian dishes instead.
food_card: Hum log shudh shakahari hai. Maas, machhli, anda nahi. Pyaaz, lahsun, aloo, gajar aur jameen ke neeche wali sabzi nahi. Dhanyavaad.
